alternativas.feedback: Correto. Sister chromatids are separated from each other following the breakdown of cohesive proteins holding them together at the centromere. Chromatids are then drawn to opposite poles by the pushing force of the polar microtubules and the pulling force of the kinetochore microtubules. Once separated, chromatids are referred to as chromosomes.
